podcast.body: Nirvana's first Sub Pop single was a cover of a song originally recorded by the Dutch band Shocking Blue. The demo version was recorded when the band was still known as "Ed Ted Fred." "Which in case you didn't know, is a cover of a song by a Dutch band called Shocking Blue."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Nirvana's first ever single, performed at Dave Grohl's first official gig with the band at the North Shore Surf Club in Olympia, Washington, on October 11, 1990. Audio from this performance is available, capturing a significant moment in the band's history with their new drummer. "This is Dave girls first show with Nirvana performing Love Buzz, the band's first ever single."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The authentic first single by Nirvana, released in October 1988 on Sub Pop Records, can be verified by a specific handwritten message in the dead wax area. This message, in two-millimeter high letters, reads "SP-23-1. Why don't you trade those guitars for shovels? L-31540." For additional proof of authenticity, holding the record up to the light should reveal the faintly machine-stamped word "K-Disk" on both sides. "And the way you can tell if you have an authentic copy of the very first Nirvana single, issued on subpop records in October of 1988, is to look for a message handwritten in letters two millimeters high."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
